newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone seen hitting Australia on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone seen hitting Australia on Wednesday.

text.p: A cyclone causing winds of up to 170 km an hour and stretching 1,000 km wide across the central Coral Sea is expected to reach the coast of Queensland, Australia on Wednesday, the Bureau of Meteorology said on Monday.

Cyclone Justin, located about 580 kms east of the resort city of Cairns, was generating waves up to five metres high as it inched toward the coastline, Bureau of Meteorology weather forecaster Jeffrey Crane said.
"It's near-stationary but appears to be building in intensity," Crane said. "It will likely be Wednesday before it reaches the coast."
Justin was larger in area than most cyclones that made their way to the Queensland coast this time of year, Crane said.
However, it was doubtful Justin would reach the intensity of previous cyclones that have devastated coastal communities in Australia.

Although it is larger, Justin lacked the "punch" of cyclone Tracy, which killed at least 65 people in 1974 when it ripped through Darwin in Australia's Northern Territory, Crane said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
